class_wall.statement: Published gRefCOCO val numbers are from models TRAINED on gRefCOCO train. The training-free wall binds on three independently measured axes: (1) grounder - the VLM box overlaps the 2-object GT union at IoU 0.329; (2) selector - under a PERFECT (GT) box the best deployable rule reaches only r=0.507 cumulative, below the r>0.689 the cIoU floor needs even at perfect abstention, so it fails at ANY N_acc (oracle on the same candidates: r=0.740, needing N_acc>=0.912; perfect single-mask oracle: r=0.581); (3) abstention - the VLM's own `none` answer reaches N_acc=0.413 (T_acc 1.000), while even the oracle-with-perfect-box ceiling needs N_acc>=0.74 for gIoU - above the 0.797 the trained state of the art reports. Note 92% of val no-target sentences are transplanted from other images, so the absences are genuine but the phrases stay generic, which is why image-grounded existence tops out near 0.41.

axis2_ceilings.note: oracle = GT-guided greedy union over the same shortlist

decomposition.verdict: Three independent axes, all measured, all short. (1) Grounder: the VLM box overlaps the 2-object union at 0.329. (2) Selector: even given a PERFECT box the best deployable rule reaches r=0.507 vs the oracle's 0.740 - and r=0.507 cannot clear cIoU at ANY N_acc. (3) Abstention: the cIoU floor at the oracle-with-perfect-box ceiling still needs N_acc>=0.91, and gIoU needs >=0.74; the best training-free existence signal measures 0.413 and the trained state of the art is 0.797. No realizable combination clears either line, and the only configurations that could would require simultaneously a perfect grounder, an oracle selector, and a trained-level abstention rate.
